## Purpose
Transport-neutral infrastructure shared by every run transport (the transitional WebSocket endpoint and the REST/SSE endpoints): the per-run event-queue/task/cancel-event registries, the SSE multi-subscriber fan-out bus, auto-resume registrar hooks wired onto the engine at startup, and the untrusted-ingress validators (images, model overrides, persisted selections) that gate a run before it launches.

## Shape
- `_PIPELINE_QUEUES` / `_PIPELINE_TASKS` / `_CANCEL_EVENTS` — the core per-run registries; `_get_or_create_queue`, `_cleanup_pipeline`, and `_is_run_live` manage their lifecycle, with `_is_run_live` self-healing a stale registration (a driver that died before its own cleanup ran) using the task's `done()` state as the sole liveness signal.
- The SSE fan-out bus (`_SUBSCRIBERS`, `_subscribe`/`_unsubscribe`/`_evict_subscriber`, `_dispatch_event_to_subscribers`) — gives each SSE client its own queue fed by a shared per-run "pump" (`_pump_run_events`/`_ensure_pump`), replacing an earlier single-queue model that silently round-robin-split events across concurrent tabs; queues are generation-tagged (`_QUEUE_GENERATIONS`) so a resumed run's new producer queue is never confused with a stale one under the same `run_id`.
- `_register_resume_queue` / `_resume_cancel_event` / `_register_resume_task` — the app-layer half of the auto-resume bridge, injected onto the engine instance at startup so an auto-resumed run is discoverable by reconnect/cancel just like a freshly-launched one.
- `_validate_model_overrides` / `_validate_images` / `_revalidate_selections_trust_user` — untrusted-payload validation chokepoints: allow-list model ids/agent ids, cap and MIME/vision-guard image uploads, and re-compile persisted per-step capability selections under `trust="user"` to catch tampering after save.
- `_authenticate_token`, `_review_gate_owned_by`, `_review_gate_run_is_terminal`, `_resolve_owned_parent_run_id` — auth/ownership guards shared by the run-command endpoints.

## Why this shape
The module deliberately imports no FastAPI transport surface so both the legacy WebSocket endpoint and the REST/SSE endpoints can share one infrastructure layer during the WS-to-REST/SSE migration; nearly every non-trivial function's docstring documents a specific race or leak it was written to close (e.g. the generation-tagged fan-out bus fixing a round-robin event-split bug, the liveness self-heal fixing permanently-stuck runs), making the file read as an incident-driven hardening log as much as infrastructure code.
